policy_name: Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024
question: What specific reporting requirements will federal law enforcement agencies and crime laboratories face to demonstrate their adherence to the Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 concerning computational forensic software?
answer_low_temp: Federal law enforcement agencies and crime laboratories using computational forensic software will be required to conduct an internal validation according to the requirements outlined in the Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Standards (Section 2(c)). The results of this internal validation must be publicly available. The Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Standards will include requirements for reports provided to defendants by prosecution, documenting the use and results of computational forensic software used in individual cases (Section 2(a)(2)(E)). These reports must include the name of the company that developed the software, the name of the lab where the test was run, the version of the software that was used, the dates of the most recent changes to the software and record of changes made, documentation of procedures followed based on procedures outlined in internal validation, documentation of conditions under which software was used relative to the conditions under which software was tested, and any other information specified by the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology in the Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Standards (Section 2(f)).
answer_high_temp: 1) Federal law enforcement agencies and crime laboratories must use software that has been tested under the National Institute of Standards and Technology's Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Program (Section 2c). 2) They must conduct an internal validation according to the requirements outlined in the Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Standards and make the results publicly available (Section 2c). 3) The internal validation shall be updated when there is a material change in the software that triggers a retesting by the Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Program (Section 2e). 4) Results or reports resulting from analysis by computational forensic software shall be provided to the defendant, including an executable copy of and the source code for the version of the computational forensic software used, as well as relevant files and data (Section 2f). 5) The report on the results shall include specific information such as the name of the company that developed the software, the name of the lab where the test was run, the version of the software that was used, and other details specified by the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology in the Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Standards (Section 2f).

policy_name: Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024
question: Under the Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024, what are the procedural steps and conditions that trigger a retesting of computational forensic software by the National Institute of Standards and Technology?
answer_low_temp:
1. Under the Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is required to establish a Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Program (Section 2(d)).

2. The testing program shall test individual software programs using the testing requirements established in the Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Standards (Section 2(d)(1)).

3. Retesting shall be conducted when a material change is made to the software that impacts its performance and may affect its outputs (Section 2(e)).

4. The Director of NIST shall establish requirements for determining whether changes are material or nonmaterial (Section 2(e)).

5. The Act does not specify the exact conditions that trigger a retesting, but it does require that testing data should represent diversity of racial, ethnic, and gender identities and intersections of these identities (Section 2(d)(3)). It also requires testing data that tests the limits of the software and demonstrates the boundaries of reliability (Section 2(d)(4)).

Sources:
- Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 (BILL)
- https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/senate-bill/3611/text
- Accessed on 2023-03-20.
answer_high_temp: 1) The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) shall establish a Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Program to test computational forensic software. 2) Retesting shall be conducted when a material change is made to the software that impacts its performance and may affect its outputs. 3) The Director shall establish requirements for determining whether changes are material or nonmaterial. (Section 2(d), (e) of the Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024)

policy_name: Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024
question: How does the Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 ensure that developers of computational forensic software provide sufficient transparency regarding their algorithms and testing methodologies to facilitate independent validation and defense access?
answer_low_temp:
The Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 ensures that developers of computational forensic software provide sufficient transparency regarding their algorithms and testing methodologies to facilitate independent validation and defense access in several ways:

1. Testing Standards (Section 2(a)(2)(C)): Developers are required to publicly document the purpose and function of the software, the development process, including source and description of data used to develop the tool, and internal testing methodology and results, including source and description of testing data.

2. Internal Validation Requirements (Section 2(c)): Federal law enforcement agencies and crime laboratories must validate computational forensic software for use, specifying the conditions under which the lab has validated it for their use, requirements for what information needs to be included in a public report on the lab or other entity’s validation, and requirements for internal validation updates when there are material changes to the software.

3. Public Reporting (Section 2(d)(5)): The results of testing the software online, including results under conditions specified in the testing standards and across diversity of racial, ethnic, and gender identities and intersections of these identities, must be published in a publicly available format.

4. Access to Software and Relevant Files (Section 2(f)): Defendants shall be accorded access to both an executable copy of and the source code for the version of the computational forensic software used for analysis in the case, as well as earlier versions of the software, necessary instructions for use and interpretation of the results, and relevant files and data.

5. Inadmissibility of Certain Evidence (Section 2(g)): Evidence that is the result of analysis by computational forensic software is admissible only if the computational forensic software used has been submitted to the Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Program of the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and there have been no material changes to that software since it was last tested.

Sources:
- Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 (BILL)
- Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure
- Federal Rules of Evidence
- Section 553 of title 5, United States Code (Administrative Procedure Act)
answer_high_temp: 1) The Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 requires developers of computational forensic software to publicly document the purpose and function of the software, the development process, and internal testing methodology and results, including source and description of data used to develop the tool (Section 2(a)(2)(C)). 2) Developers must also make an executable copy of and the source code for the version of the computational forensic software, as well as earlier versions, necessary instructions for use and interpretation of the results, and relevant files and data, available to defendants for testing purposes (Section 2(f)). 3) The Act establishes a Computational Forensic Algorithm Testing Program to test software using realistic sample testing data and publishing the results online in a publicly available format (Section 2(d)).

policy_name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 248 ("Pilot program on self-directed training in advanced technologies")
question: What specific procedures will the Secretary of Defense establish for the development, selection, approval, adoption, and evaluation of online courses to ensure they align with the pilot program's goals and the broader training needs of the Department of Defense workforce?
answer_low_temp:
The Secretary of Defense will establish procedures for the development, selection, approval, adoption, and evaluation of online courses under Section 248(b) of the Act. These procedures may include:

1. Development: The Secretary may create a process for the development of online courses by subject matter experts, industry professionals, and educational institutions.

2. Selection: The Secretary may establish criteria for selecting online courses that align with the goals of the pilot program and the broader training needs of the Department of Defense workforce. These criteria may include relevance to advanced technologies, applicability to job-related functions, and alignment with mission requirements.

3. Approval: The Secretary may establish a review process to approve online courses that meet the selection criteria. This process may involve review by subject matter experts, educational institutions, and relevant departments within the Department of Defense.

4. Adoption: The Secretary may establish a process for making approved online courses available to civilian employees and members of the Armed Forces. This process may involve integration with existing training platforms or the creation of a new platform.

5. Evaluation: The Secretary may establish metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of the online courses in improving the ability of participants to perform job-related functions and execute relevant missions of the Department of Defense (Section 248(e)). This evaluation may involve surveys, assessments, and performance metrics.

Citation: Title II, Subtitle A, Section 248, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Public Law 116-283)

Lastly, the Secretary will develop metrics to evaluate the impact of these courses on the ability of participants to perform job-related functions and execute relevant Department of Defense missions (Sec. 248(e)).

policy_name: Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025 (Sec. 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership.")
question: What are the specific criteria and processes the Secretaries will use to ensure that selected covered entities are effectively testing technologies for wildfire mitigation and that these tests align with the identified key technology priority areas?
answer_low_temp:
1. The Secretaries will establish a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies (SEC. 302(b)).

2. The Secretaries, in consultation with the heads of covered agencies, will identify key technology priority areas with respect to the deployment of wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies (SEC. 302(c)(2)). These priority areas include hazardous fuels reduction activities or treatments, dispatch communications, remote sensing and tracking, safety equipment, and common operating pictures or operational dashboards.

3. To participate in the Pilot Program, a covered entity must submit an application to the Secretaries, which should include a proposal to test technologies specific to the key technology priority areas identified under subsection (c)(2) (SEC. 302(d)).

4. The Secretaries will give priority to covered entities developing and applying emerging technologies that address issues identified by the Secretaries, including artificial intelligence, quantum sensing, computing and quantum-hybrid applications, augmented reality, and 5G private networks and device-to-device communications supporting nomadic mesh networks, for wildfire mitigation (SEC. 302(e)).

5. The Secretaries will connect each covered entity selected to participate in the Pilot Program with the appropriate covered agency to coordinate real-time and on-the-ground testing of technology during wildland fire mitigation activities and training (SEC. 302(c)(3)).

6. The Secretaries will make publicly available the key technology priority areas identified under subsection (c)(2) and invite covered entities to apply to test and demonstrate their technologies to address those priority areas (SEC. 302(f)).

7. The Secretaries will submit an annual report to the appropriate committees, which includes a list of participating covered entities, a brief description of the technologies tested by such covered entities, an estimate of the cost of acquiring the technology tested in the Pilot Program and applying it at scale, outreach efforts by Federal agencies to covered entities developing wildfire technologies, assessments of, and recommendations relating to, new technologies with potential adoption and application at-scale in the wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation efforts of Federal land management agencies (SEC. 302(g)).

8. The Pilot Program
answer_high_temp: 1) The Secretaries will establish a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies (Section b). 2) Key technology priority areas will be identified in consultation with the heads of covered agencies (Section c(2)). 3) Covered entities selected to participate in the Pilot Program will coordinate real-time and on-the-ground testing of technology during wildland fire mitigation activities and training with the appropriate covered agency (Section c(3)). 4) Priority will be given to covered entities developing and applying emerging technologies that address issues identified by the Secretaries, including artificial intelligence (Section e). 5) The Secretaries will make publicly available the key technology priority areas and invite covered entities to apply to test and demonstrate their technologies to address those priority areas (Section f).

policy_name: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act
question: What specific procedures will the Center employ to identify and resolve conflicts that arise between the various executive departments and agencies involved in export control enforcement and licensing?
answer_low_temp:
The Export Enforcement Coordination Center, as established by S. 4085, will employ the following procedures to identify and resolve conflicts that arise between the various executive departments and agencies involved in export control enforcement and licensing:

1. The Center will serve as the primary forum within the Federal Government for executive departments and agencies to coordinate and enhance their export control enforcement efforts (Sec. 2(c)(1)).
2. The Center will identify and resolve conflicts that have not been otherwise resolved in criminal and administrative investigations and actions involving violations of the export control laws of the United States (Sec. 2(c)(1)(B)).
3. The Director of the Center will convene and preside at meetings of the Center, determine the agenda for those meetings, direct the work of the Center, and, as appropriate to particular subject matters, organize and coordinate subgroups of the members of the Center (Sec. 2(d)(1)(B)).

5. The Center will coordinate law enforcement public outreach activities related to United States export controls (Sec. 2(c)(4)).
6. The Center will establish governmentwide statistical tracking capabilities for United States criminal and administrative export control enforcement activities (Sec. 2(c)(5)).

Sources:

answer_high_temp: The Center will serve as the primary forum for executive departments and agencies to coordinate and enhance their export control enforcement efforts, identify and resolve conflicts that have not been otherwise resolved in criminal and administrative investigations and actions involving violations of the export control laws of the United States (Section 2(c)(1)). The Director of the Center will convene and preside at meetings of the Center, determine the agenda for those meetings, direct the work of the Center, and as appropriate, organize and coordinate subgroups of the members of the Center (Section 2(d)(1)(B)).

policy_name: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act
question: Describe the governmentwide statistical tracking capabilities the Center will establish, and how will the data collected from participating departments and agencies be used to assess and improve export control enforcement activities?
answer_low_temp: The Export Enforcement Coordination Center, established under the Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024, will establish governmentwide statistical tracking capabilities for United States criminal and administrative export control enforcement activities (Sec. 2(c)(5)). This data will be collected from participating departments and agencies (Sec. 2(c)(5)) and used to conduct statistical tracking by the Department of Homeland Security (Sec. 2(c)(5)). The collected data will help assess and improve export control enforcement activities by providing a comprehensive overview of the enforcement efforts across various departments and agencies, enabling the identification of trends, gaps, and areas for improvement in export control enforcement (Sec. 2(c)(5)).
answer_high_temp: The Center will establish governmentwide statistical tracking capabilities for United States criminal and administrative export control enforcement activities, to be conducted by the Department of Homeland Security with information provided by and shared with all relevant departments and agencies participating in the Center. The data collected will be used to assess and improve export control enforcement activities by identifying trends, patterns, and potential areas of concern, allowing for more effective coordination and enforcement efforts among participating agencies. (Reference: S. 4085, Section 2(c)(5))
